div.l: He waited aftre no pompe nor reuerens
Nor he made him not a spiced countenaunce
But cristes lorde and his appostoles . xij .
He taught but first he foloued it him selue
With him þere was a ploghman his owne brother
That had lad of dong mani a fother
A trewe swinker and a good was he
Leueyng in pees and in charite
God loued he best with al his hert
At al tyme þough him gamed or smert
And þan his neghbourgh as him self
He wold tressh and thereto dig and delf
For cristes sake to eueri pouer wight
With oute hir if it lai in his might
His tithes paied he ful faire and wele
Both of his propre swink and of his catell
In A tabard he rode vpon a mere
There was also a reve and a myller
A sompnour and a ꝑpardoner aso
A mansipe and my self þere was no mo
The myller was a strought cherle for þe nones
Full bigge he was of braune and of bones
That proues well for ouer all þere wher he came
At wresteling he wold haue þe rame
He was short shuldered and a thik knarr
Ther was no dore þat he nold haue an harre
Wel wist he be þe droght and be þe reyne
The yeldyngꝭes of his sede and of his greyne
His lordꝭes nete his shepe his daiery
His somer his horse his store and his pultrie
Was holi in þis reues goủernyng
And bi his couenaunt yaf rekenyng
Sithen his lorde was xx winter of age
Ther couth no man̄ bring him in rerage
Ther nas bailif herd nor oþer hyne
That he ne knewe his sleght and his couyne
Thei were a drad for him as for þe dethe
His wonnyng was ful fair vpon an heth
With grene trees shadowed was his place
He couth better þan his lorde purchace
Ful riche he was a stored priveli
His lorde he couth plese skilfulli
To lene and gif him of his own gode
